- **Authority and source:** Resolution R-26-7, "Providing for a Temporary Moratorium on the Acceptance of Applications Relating to the Establishment, Operation or Expansion of Data Centers, Nuclear Power Generation Facilities, Hydrogen-Based Energy Facilities, and Battery Energy Storage Systems within the Unincorporated Areas of Neosho County," adopted and signed 2026-05-19 by Chairman Gail Klaassen, citing K.S.A. 19-101 et seq. police power.
- **What prompted it:** The Neosho County Commission had already developed regulations for wind, commercial-scale solar, and battery energy storage, but had received no applications for data centers, nuclear power generation, hydrogen-based energy, or (further) battery storage facilities; commissioners wanted time to review and potentially adopt land development regulations for these uses before any applications arrived.
- **Affected projects:** No applications for the covered uses had been submitted in unincorporated Neosho County as of adoption.
- **Status notes:** Signed May 19, 2026 resolution provides for a moratorium through June 1, 2027, subject to change, effective upon adoption and publication. Publication and subsequent action were not obtained; current force is unverified.
- **Outcome:** Suspends acceptance/processing of building permits, site plan/architectural reviews, variances, floodplain permits, conditional use permits, grading permits, rezoning applications, and occupancy permits for data centers, nuclear power generation facilities, hydrogen-based energy facilities, and battery energy storage systems in unincorporated Neosho County during the moratorium period, while the Commission reviews potential regulations.

### HB 2433 floor amendment (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `ks-hb-2433-floor-amendment-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Michael Murphy amendment; Sen. Chase Blasi publicly supported drought-county pause per Wichita Eagle; Republican
- **Status:** Sen. Michael Murphy's Committee of the Whole floor amendment was ruled germane and rejected on 2026-03-12. The separate underlying HB 2433 passed the Senate 36-3 with one absent on 2026-03-13, was enrolled 2026-03-17 and approved by the Governor 2026-03-20.
- **Provisions:** The rejected amendment proposed prohibiting installation, placement, construction or operation of new data centers reasonably expected to have monthly maximum demand of at least 10 MW in counties with a drought emergency declared within the preceding three calendar years; it required county denial and permitted a county moratorium during that period, with specified grandfathering and preservation of more restrictive local rules. Similarity to SB 531 and the Wichita Eagle's reported 12-22 vote remain qualified leads; the reviewed journal records rejection without a tally.
- **Mechanism / scope:** permitting_restriction; statewide
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** Proposed restriction applies during the three-calendar-year period following a county drought-emergency declaration; the proposed county moratorium could last until the end of that period.
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://www.kslegislature.gov/b2025_26/bills/download/?apn=b2025_26/year2/ready_for_publication/floor_amendments/4258/fa_2026_hb2433_s_4258.pdf>)
